arguments.value: 38-year-old woman with a history of migraines, chronic anemia, and heavy menstrual flows presented with 1 week of constant severe headache and 3 weeks of right eye vision changes, including loss of vision, pain with eye movement, diplopia, ptosis, and right-sided facial numbness/tingling. Exam showed right ptosis and right-gaze palsy with restricted horizontal eye movements. CT and MRI demonstrated a 3.2 cm dilatation of the right internal carotid artery consistent with a thrombosed aneurysm. She was monitored with hourly neurologic checks, head-of-bed elevation, aspirin, dexamethasone, and blood pressure control, with angiography and surgical/non-surgical options under consideration.
